newsitem.title: USA: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.
newsitem.headline: National carlot beef trade weekly review - USDA.

text.p: Boxed beef trading was uneven on light to moderate demand and offerings during the interrupted New Years holiday week, USDA said.

Retail and HRI demand was for immediate needs, while forward interest was rather light. The light Choice and Select spread continues to tighten and presently stands at $5.25, which is the smallest week ending spread since Sep.19.

Rib and loin cuts were responsible for the tightening as holiday buying for those cuts ended. Choice rib cuts traded sharply lower as these cuts lost some of their holiday premium, while Select rib cuts traded steady.
Choice loin cuts traded lower, while Select loin cuts traded higher as these cuts were seen as better values compared to their Choice counterparts.
Chuck and round cuts traded steady throughout the trading period; however, some chuck cuts ended on a weak undertone.

Closely trimmed items traded uneven on light to moderate demand with Choice product trading lower, while Select product was generally steady. Trade on beef trimmings was weak on light to moderate demand and offerings. Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items were steady to higher on light to moderate demand and offerings.
Most of the advances on the grinds occurred early in the trading period.

For the week - Select rib primal generally steady, Choice rib primal 9.00 to 10.00 lower; Select and Choice chuck primal generally steady; Select and Choice round primal generally steady; Select loin primal 4.00 to 6.00 higher, Choice loin primal 2.00 to 2.50 lower; Closely trimmed items steady to 2.00 lower; Beef trimmings 1.50 lower; Fed cattle and blended coarse ground items steady to 2.00 higher.

The Estimated Composite of Boxed Beef Cutout values of Choice 1-3 550/700 carcasses Dn 2.45 at 105.15; 700/850 Dn 1.53 at 104.67; Select 1-3 550/700 carcasses Up 1.22 at 99.90; 700/850 Up .39 at 98.79.

COW AND BULL CARCASS, BONELESS PROCESSING BEEF, CUTTER COW CUTOUT Production continued to be curtailed by the holiday season. However, demand was good early in the week and lean boneless beef traded higher. Consequently, as the week progressed demand became light and offerings increased and a lower undertone was noted.

Cow cuts were lightly traded with some firmness noted on the 100% lean flats and eyes. Utility carcasses no recent test for comparison; Cutter carcasses not established; Fresh 90% boneless beef generally 1.50-2.50 higher in the Midwest, Texas mostly 5.00 higher; 85% firm; 75% steady; 65% generally steady. The Cutter cow carcass gross cut-out value for Thursday, January 2, 1996 was estimated at 73.83 per cwt., up 1.32 from a week ago Friday.
